correctness.rationale: Direct Fourier moments on the two m-gons give diagonal 1 and the only nonzero off-diagonals at k−l=±m, conjugates with modulus s=|sin(mδ)|. The resulting m blocks give the claimed spectrum, including coincident eigenvalues at δ=0. Rotation by 2π/m and reflection about π/N act transitively; conjugation or conjugate-unitary equivalence preserves the Loewner bounds and the Frobenius objective. Averaging therefore gives both individual eigenvalue bounds and the condition bound for every normalized positive vector. Vandermonde injectivity makes the squared defect strictly convex in the weights, and det G=|det A|² prod w_j gives precisely the unique AM–GM equality case. At any total mass t the unique equal-weight minimum is N[(t−1)²+t²s²], whose minimizer is t=1/(1+s²). The endpoints leave m distinct nodes with Vandermonde rank m; expansion of cos(π(1/2−|α|)) gives the claimed condition divergence. The direct moment argument bypasses the transpose convention in the displayed 2-by-2 evaluation block.
residual_risks: No claim outside the exact consecutive-frequency, two-coset setting or beyond the displayed rigidity statements.

value.rationale: A natural periodic test of critically sampled Fourier stability gives the exact improvement ceiling for every positive density compensation, not merely a uniform spectrum or perturbative bound. The saturation and divergence at collision and the optimal tradeoff when mass may shrink give usable benchmarks for reweighting objectives.
residual_risks: The design benchmark does not extend to arbitrary jitter or different frequency/sample counts by this argument.
